note: Parks Canada campground on the Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93N), 91 km north of the Highway 1/93N junction in Banff National Park, across from the Rampart Creek Hostel; treed sites backing onto the North Saskatchewan River banks. Only 3 sites take a rig over 27 ft and 22 take one up to 24 ft; some loops are unsuitable over 8 m. Solar-treated drinking water but no RV fill: fill and dump at Waterfowl Lakes Campground, 32 km south. No cell coverage. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: 51 unserviced reservation-only sites, C$22 a night plus Banff entry; 2026 season May 28 - Sep 20 (stored 05-20..09-15 was note-derived). Fees (entrance, max 6 people, fire-permit note), sites (35 ft max, none pull-through), hookups, facilities, season, booking written; note rewritten (the old '~12 km N of Saskatchewan River Crossing' dropped for the page's own location line).
flags: PHONE (stored empty): no campground-specific number on Parks Canada's pages or the reservation service's location record. The Banff contact page (200) gives Lake Louise Visitor Centre 403-522-3833 (covers the Lake Louise area and Icefields Parkway), Banff Visitor Centre 403-762-1550, reservations 1-877-737-3783. Recommend 403-522-3833.

WEBSITE: the Banff camping page answered 200. reservation.pc.gc.ca answers 403 (Azure WAF) to plain fetches; in the browser this campground's catalogue (resourceLocationId -2147483639) was read in full. Deep link: https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/create-booking/results?resourceLocationId=-2147483639&mapId=-2147483648

FIT: a 23-ft rig fits only the sites allowing 'up to 24ft' or more: 22 of 51 (3 up to 35 ft, 9 up to 27 ft, 10 up to 24 ft). 16 sites are capped at 21 ft and 13 are tent/walk-in only. Main pads are mostly 13-20 ft long. Keep, but the fit is tight; reviewer may want the caveat (it is in the note).

MAX LENGTH: page 'up to 10 meters (35 feet)', 'some loops are not suitable ... over 8 meters (25 feet)'; catalogue agrees (3 sites to 35 ft). 35 written (stored 33 was note-derived). Note the page's general Banff table line elsewhere is not given for Rampart.
FACILITIES: drinking water exists but 'no RV fill' - potable_water left unwritten (same call as Silverhorn 8804 in p3-374).

POLICY ROW (federal:parks-canada) CONTRADICTION: the row says 'Fire permits are extra where sold (Banff C$12-17 a day)'. Here the page says 'Reservations include fire permits, where applicable', and 46 drive-in sites are service type 'Unserviced with on-site Fire Pit (Fire Permit Added)' (the 5 walk-ins 'Walk-in, Unserviced with on-site Fire Pit (Fire Permit Added)'). The C$17/day permit looks bundled into every booking - about C$39 a night booked (22 + 17). Whether the cart actually charges it per night is UNREAD (no quote taken).

WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront - keep; observation): the page says 'The campground backs onto the banks of the North Saskatchewan River with impressive views of the river valley'. Esri imagery (0.4-0.67 m/px): the campground is under continuous conifer canopy; the only openings near the river are two small buildings (shelters) about 60-80 m from the water across a forested strip and a gravel bar. The site spurs visible through the canopy are about 150-250 m from the river with forest between. No pads meet the ~50 m open-ground test; nothing confirmable for river view under canopy. Recommend not waterfront.

PIN: stored 52.04007,-116.86979 is in the forest at the western (river) side of the campground, roughly 150 m from the loops; the reservation service's location gives 52.04206,-116.86776 (on the loop road, ~270 m NNE) and Google's directions link 52.03908,-116.86748. Within the campground footprint; no move (reviewer may prefer 52.0414,-116.8680, the loop centre).
PROTECTION/RAMPART season: 2026 go-live for Rampart was in the row's window (reservation date schedule). Max stay 14 nights from the Banff page.
